newsitem.title: POLAND: FLEMINGS SEES NFI UNITS WORTH PLN 150-160.
newsitem.headline: FLEMINGS SEES NFI UNITS WORTH PLN 150-160.

text.p: National Investment Fund (NFI) units in Poland's mass privatisation programme should be valued at 150 to 160 zlotys, Flemings' latest Global Emerging Markets report said.
Under the Polish government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.
From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme have been entitled to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which start trade on the Warsaw bourse on June 12.
The units, which closed on the bourse on Thursday at 152 zlotys, lose their validity on December 31, 1998.

"As the certificates, which we currently value at around 150-160 zlotys, will continue to be traded...there will be an arbitrage between the two investments," the report said, referring to the units and separate funds.
Flemings also said the funds would become an alternative investment pool for new money, particularly for more speculative domestic investors.
